title: Symmetric DNA Strand Checker
description:
A genetics laboratory analyzes raw DNA sequencing data stored as strings. Due to noise during scanning, readings often contain non-essential characters such as digits, whitespace, and special punctuation.

A valid nucleotide base is represented by the characters 'A', 'C', 'G', or 'T' (case-insensitive, so 'a', 'c', 'g', 't' are also valid base readings).

Your task is to determine whether the sequence of valid nucleotide bases forms a symmetric pattern (reads the same from left-to-right as right-to-left), ignoring all non-base noise characters. An empty sequence of valid bases is considered symmetric.
constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters.
input_format: A single string s representing the raw sequencing data.
output_format: Return true if the filtered nucleotide base sequence is symmetric, or false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Ignoring non-base characters and normalizing case gives the nucleotide sequence "ACGTGCA". Reading from left-to-right or right-to-left yields "ACGTGCA", which is symmetric.
After ignoring all noise characters, the resulting nucleotide sequence is empty. An empty sequence is considered symmetric by definition.
Filtering the string gives the nucleotide sequence "ATCGTA". Reading backwards yields "ATGCTA". Since "ATCGTA" does not equal "ATGCTA", the strand is not symmetric.
